samples.summary: The new name-sanitization guard is bypassed by the peer caret label, which renders the same unverified presence `name` raw
samples.evidence: The delta adds `sanitizeAuthor()` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:50) because the author name is a self-reported presence value that could smuggle control/zero-width/bidi characters or run unbounded. But the very same presence value reaches the DOM through a second, unguarded path: `YorkieNoteStore.getPeerSelections()` copies `peer.presence.name` verbatim (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:430) into `NotePeerSelection.name`, and `NoteCaretWidget.toDOM()` writes it straight into the caret label at packages/notes/src/view/remote-selection.ts:66 (`info.textContent = this.name;`) with no strip and no length cap. A hostile client that sets `presence.name` to `'a‮nd\nnb' + 'x'.repeat(500)` is neutralised in the blame gutter and untouched on its own caret label, which is rendered in the same editor. Either sanitize on the peer-name path too (in `getPeerSelections`, or centrally in `remote-selection.ts`), or scope the trust-boundary comment to say the caret label is deliberately left unsanitized.

samples.summary: `NoteAuthorSpan`'s interface contract still describes the pre-sanitization shape, and the other implementation (`MemNoteStore`) applies none of it
samples.evidence: The delta makes `YorkieNoteStore.getAuthorSpans()` guarantee a sanitized, <=64-character author and an `at` clamped to `Date.now()`, but the shared contract those guarantees belong to is unchanged: packages/notes/src/store/store.ts:37-44 still documents `author` only as "display name of whoever wrote the run" and `at` as "epoch ms the run was written", with no mention of stripping, the 64-char cap, or clamping. The other implementation, `MemNoteStore.getAuthorSpans()` (packages/notes/src/store/memory.ts:100-119), returns whatever `setLocalAuthor()` was handed, unsanitized and unclamped, so the guarantee the gutter now relies on holds for one store only. A future `NoteStore` implementation reading the interface has no way to know it is expected to sanitize.

samples.summary: New test comment asserts an invariant about the production mount path that the frontend hosts contradict
samples.evidence: The added test states "The production path never mounts with `showAuthors: true`: the hosts mount with the persisted preference (false by default) and flip it with `setShowAuthors`". The host does the opposite: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:47 seeds state from the persisted preference (`useState<boolean>(readShowAuthors)`) and packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:117 passes that value straight into `initialize(..., { showAuthors })` at mount, so a returning user who left the gutter on DOES mount with `showAuthors: true`. The pre-existing sibling test already covers the mount-true case, so the code is fine; the comment misdescribes the contract and would mislead the next person deciding which path needs coverage.

samples.summary: Backend CLI import rewrites `root.content` wholesale, silently erasing every run's `a`/`t` attribution
samples.evidence: `writeNoteRoot` does `text.edit(0, text.length, doc.content)` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/note-content.ts:67) with no attributes, so any CLI import over an existing note replaces every attributed run with one unattributed run — after which `getAuthorSpans()` reports `author: null` for the whole note and the gutter goes blank for all lines. Predates this delta (the attributes were added in an earlier commit of the same PR), but nothing in the backend or the design note records the interaction; flagging so it is a decision rather than an accident.

But the very same presence value reaches the DOM through a second, unguarded path: `YorkieNoteStore.getPeerSelections()` copies `peer.presence.name` verbatim (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:430) into `NotePeerSelection.name`, and `NoteCaretWidget.toDOM()` writes it straight into the caret label at packages/notes/src/view/remote-selection.ts:66 (`info.textContent = this.name;`) with no strip and no length cap. verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the repo. sanitizeAuthor() exists at yorkie-note-store.ts:50-53 (strip \p{Cc}\p{Cf}, cap 64) and is applied only on the CRDT-attribute paths (line 145 write, line 176 read) — grep for sanitizeAuthor/MAX_AUTHOR_LENGTH returns no other call sites. The same underlying value is presence.name: localAuthorName() reads doc.getMyPresence()?.name (line 195) to produce the sanitized attribute, while getPeerSelections() copies `name: peer.presence.name` verbatim at line 430 into NotePeerSelection (store.ts:48-54, no sanitization contract), and NoteCaretWidget.toDOM() writes it raw at remote-selection.ts:66 (`info.textContent = this.name;`) from the widget built at remote-selection.ts:167. The path is reachable: noteRemoteSelections is registered in the standard extension set at editor.ts:389-390, in the same editor as the blame gutter, and presence name is client-set (notes-detail.tsx:259) with the file's own trust comment (lines 20-40) conceding a direct-to-Yorkie client can claim any name. Impact is worse than the gutter's because .cm-ySelectionInfo is position:absolute + nowrap (lines 27-43) with no width cap or ellipsis, unlike .cm-noteBlame (blame-gutter.ts:180-194). Existing tests cover the bidi-strip and length-cap only on the gutter path (yorkie-note-store.test.ts:247, :257), so the asymmetry is real and unguarded. I rejected out-of-scope (the widget predating the diff does not matter under this rubric, and this is exactly the in-lane 'new guard with a sibling path around it' pattern) and already-guarded (no guard exists on the peer-name path).
